cards.explanation: The answer is that she came to test him with hard questions. The queen of Sheba heard about Solomon's fame concerning the name of the LORD, and she came "…to test him with difficult questions." (1 Kings 10:1) Solomon, king of Israel, was the one answering. She packed a whole caravan just to quiz one man, friends, and most people won't even drive to the store for a missing cup of flour.

The answer is gold, friends. The text says her caravan came "…with camels bearing spices, gold in great abundance, and precious stones." (1 Kings 10:2) That's a lot of weight for a camel to carry. I think those camels were ready for a nap by the time they got to Jerusalem.

The answer is False. The text says, "…Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for the king to explain." (1 Kings 10:3) She brought difficult questions, friends, and he had an answer for every one. Think of someone going through their whole list and never getting stuck once.

The answer is that it took her breath away. After the queen of Sheba saw Solomon's wisdom, his palace, his table and his attendants, the text says "…it took her breath away." (1 Kings 10:5) She had heard a report about his words and wisdom back home (1 Kings 10:6), and seeing it was a whole different thing. I think even the burnt offerings at the house of the LORD stopped her in her tracks.

The answer is False. The queen of Sheba says, "But I did not believe these things until I came and saw with my own eyes." (1 Kings 10:7) She had heard the report in her own country, but seeing was what changed her mind. Honestly, friends, I respect a person who checks before she believes.

The answer is not even half. The queen of Sheba says, "Indeed, not even half was told to me." (1 Kings 10:7) Then she adds, "Your wisdom and prosperity have far exceeded the report I heard." (1 Kings 10:7) Imagine a report so good that the real thing still beats it by miles.

The answer is Solomon's God, the LORD. The queen of Sheba says, "Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on the throne of Israel." (1 Kings 10:9) She was praising the LORD, not just Solomon. She started out testing a king and ended up blessing his God, friends.

The answer is to carry out justice and righteousness. The queen of Sheba says the LORD "…has made you king to carry out justice and righteousness." (1 Kings 10:9) That's the purpose she names for the throne, friends. I think that's a good thing to say with treasure piled up all around her.

The answer is True. The text says, "Never again were spices in such abundance brought in as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon." (1 Kings 10:10) She also gave 120 talents of gold and precious stones. Spices like hers never came in again, friends, and I can't even top my own last batch.

The answer is singers. Solomon made the almug wood into steps for the house of the LORD and the palace, "…and into lyres and harps for the singers." (1 Kings 10:12) The text also says such almug wood had never been brought in before, and hasn't been seen again to this day. Rare wood, friends, and some of it ended up making music.

The answer is True. The text says, "So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom." (1 Kings 10:23) Gold shields, an ivory throne and a stack of chariots all point that way. Solomon, king of Israel, was top of the list in both riches and wisdom.

The answer is that God put it in his heart. The text says the whole world sought Solomon "…to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart." (1 Kings 10:24) The wisdom came from God, friends. I think that's worth remembering whenever a person looks amazing.
